office_open_deep_link.browser_result: chrome-error://chromewebdata/ (ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR); Next RSC prefetch also fails with 'Failed to fetch RSC payload'.
office_open_deep_link.root_cause: src/app/office/open/route.ts uses `new URL(target, url.origin)` for every NextResponse.redirect. Behind the Cloudflare/emergent proxy, the request URL that Next receives on the server is the internal bind (http://0.0.0.0:3000/…), so `url.origin` becomes 'https://0.0.0.0:3000' and the Location header points at 0.0.0.0 which the browser cannot resolve via HTTPS. Every branch (unauthenticated → /login, no-access → /office/clients, no-membership → /office/clients/<id>, success → safeTo) is affected.
office_open_deep_link.suggested_fix: Use forwarded host/proto instead of url.origin, e.g. `const proto = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto') ?? url.protocol.replace(':',''); const host = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-host') ?? req.headers.get('host') ?? url.host; const origin = `${proto}://${host}`; return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(safeTo, origin));`. Or use `req.nextUrl` (which honors Next's trusted proxy config) instead of `new URL(req.url)`.

rca_of_the_issue: In /app/frontend/src/app/office/open/route.ts line 10 `const url = new URL(req.url);` — behind the reverse proxy Next.js receives the internal request URL (http://0.0.0.0:3000/...), so `url.origin === 'http://0.0.0.0:3000'` (or https at CF layer). All 4 redirect returns build the Location as `new URL(target, url.origin)`, so the Location header becomes `https://0.0.0.0:3000/<target>`. The browser attempts an HTTPS TLS handshake against 0.0.0.0:3000 and fails with ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR. Fix by deriving the origin from `x-forwarded-proto` + `x-forwarded-host` (or `host`) headers, or use `req.nextUrl` which respects proxy trust settings.
